title: Add benchmark-lab profiling baselines and reporting pipeline (v147)
author: Evan Wright
description:
Summary: Add new profiling baselines, representative workload runners, and a reporting pipeline integration for the benchmark-lab. This PR bundles (1) profiling baselines for v1/v2 kernels, (2) a set of representative workload runners to exercise multi-variant and mixed workloads, and (3) a reporting pipeline that publishes aggregated performance metrics to the telemetry stack and BigQuery for downstream dashboards. Motivation: recent kernel changes and adaptive-batching experiments have changed tail-latency characteristics; we need stable baselines and automated reporting to detect regressions early and to keep historical comparisons consistent. Checklist:
- [x] Add profiling baseline configs and sample outputs for 4 model/seq-length combos
- [x] Implement representative workload runners (cpu/gpu variants) with deterministic seeds
- [x] Add CI job to run quick baselines on PRs and nightly full-run pipeline
- [x] Wire reporting pipeline: publish summarized metrics to telemetry service and BigQuery table benchmark_lab.metrics_v147
- [x] Add Looker/Metabase dashboard descriptors and sample queries to observability-pack
- [x] Update docs/benchmark-lab/README with how to run, expected output schema, and performance acceptance criteria

Details: The profiling baselines are implemented under benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines/v147/ and include canonical samples for: small-seq (256), med-seq (1024), long-seq (4096), and chat-like multi-turn traces. Representative runners under benchmark-lab/runners/ include: mixed_workload_runner.py, multi_variant_runner.go, and a lightweight telemetry emitter. The reporting pipeline is a new workflow under infra/ci/workflows/benchmark-reporting.yml which kicks off nightly runs, collects artifacts, runs the summarizer (benchmark-lab/tools/summarize.py), and then publishes the payload to the telemetry ingestion endpoint and to BigQuery (project:redwood-telemetry, dataset:benchmark_lab, table:metrics_v147). The PR includes feature gating so the nightly pipeline can be toggled (env var BENCHLAB_REPORTING_ENABLED). Backwards compatibility: existing baselines remain untouched; new v147 baselines live in a separate directory and do not shadow older runs. Related work: ENG-2134 (profiling baselines), ENG-2201 (reporting pipeline), SUP-987 (customer incident that motivated additional long-sequence traces).
